component.name: OpenSGolf
component.summary: Build and run your own golf resort

description.p: OpenSGolf is a free, open source engine for the golf course building game Sid Meier’s SimGolf (2002). Lay out holes, plant trees and dig ponds, put up a clubhouse and shops, hire staff, and watch your golfers play your course, chat, complain and come back for more.

It comes with its own complete set of free graphics and sounds, so you can start playing right away. If you own SimGolf, you can choose “Use my SimGolf files…” in the game and pick your installed game folder, the CD, a CD image or a .zip of the folder: OpenSGolf then plays with the original art and sounds. No game files are included.
With every option at its default it aims to play exactly like the original. On top of that it offers:

ul.li: Any window size and full screen, with optional enhanced, high-resolution graphics
Optional fixes for bugs of the original game
Optional interface helpers and extras, all off until you turn them on
A course editor for your own scenarios, and content packs (mods)
Mouse, keyboard, touch screen and game controller support

description.p: OpenSGolf is not affiliated with or endorsed by Electronic Arts or Firaxis Games. SimGolf and Sid Meier’s are trademarks of their owners and are named here only to say which game’s files OpenSGolf can use.

description.p: The view can no longer be scrolled off the map, and in full screen the pointer at the screen's edge scrolls it, as in the original.
Painting over a flower bed or a small object takes it away; a game's options stay that game's, so new games start with the ones chosen on the title screens.
Celebrities at their homes wear their own colours, and each home shows who lives there.
A green painted beside a putting green no longer joins it, and gets its flag.
Painting water over the sea keeps its depth and colour, and the pointer to the right of the build panel no longer picks a tree.
The game takes much less memory and Enhanced graphics run faster; Pause in the background also stops the sound, and Autosave saves when the game goes to the background.
The pine tree brush no longer shows a path tile under the pointer.
A first-start box helps choose how to play, and What's new is shown once after updating.
Loading a save in the browser no longer freezes for seconds, and typing in the bug report form opened from Report a problem no longer loses what you type.
Game options lists each page's most wanted options first, with Helpers split into Saves and Controls, and the title screen shows the version.
A new game's building beside the clubhouse no longer hangs over the edge of a small property.
Smoother play: the short freezes as golfers came and went are gone, and the course draws faster.

Enhanced graphics keep up better on large screens and slower machines (a browser draws them at up to 1440p and stretches them to a 4K screen), and ease off a step at a time by themselves when the game runs slowly.
Preferences can make HD graphics from your own SimGolf files, on your own device.
The free graphics' golfers have a new cast of cartoon faces, and the game says when some of your SimGolf files cannot be read.
The game now looks for a newer version when it starts and offers to install it, saying nothing if there is none (Preferences, More switches it off).
Two new options, both off until switched on: aim and swing with the mouse the way touch screens do, and no new dandelions in sandbox games.
Fixed the picture going black or jumbled after resizing or maximising the window (with multisampling, HD or some Enhanced effects on).
Classic graphics shade hills smoothly, as the original does, instead of in hard tile-sized steps.
Each theme's own buildings have their names again: the desert's Spa, Helipad and Casino, the links' Pub, Stable, Church and Castle, the parkland's Tennis Court and the tropical Theme Park.

Golfer stories play as in the original: the lines show in bubbles over the two golfers with their portraits, and a scene plays only while you watch the pair close up, instead of in a box in the middle of the screen wherever you look.
Placing a landmark, flower bed or scenic tree now places the one you chose: a click on the course no longer picks the item the pointer passed over on the way.
Paths are drawn with the original's pieces: ends and bends join up without loose round dots, and a path joined to the clubhouse is grey as in the original.
The tee of an open hole shows the original's arrow pointing the way to the hole, turning with the view.
Sand traps keep the shape you turned them to before placing them, as in the original.
Enhanced graphics: fixed a brief flash of large, blocky shadows on busy courses, and removed the twinkling white dots on the ground on spring and autumn mornings.
The tropical trees show again with retail CD installs, whose tree folders are named with spaces (Tree Cerc, Tree Drac) where other copies use underscores.
Problem reports now say why a game file could not be opened, and list what its folder holds, to track down missing pictures.

Builds from GitHub can count play time anonymously (one count per 15 minutes played, no personal data), with a notice and an off switch in Preferences. Store builds, including this one, leave it out entirely.
The support reminder now says how long you have played and what keeping OpenSGolf going costs.
The title menu and Preferences show your total time played, and option descriptions are no longer cut off on touch screens.

The Analyze Golf Shot button on the Elevation panel works: click near a hole to see golfers' sample shots. On the tropical and Links courses, the tree and stream buttons now show their own names and descriptions. A lone elm tree stands in the middle of its square again.

New Report a problem form, an optional Looks extra for the desert's Ravine and Brush art, more faithful saves (the hole plan and the calendar's hold are kept), each save checked as it is written, and, after an hour of play, a gentle note about supporting the project that asks at most twice.
On touch screens, dragging while moving an employee now scrolls the view instead of placing them.
Free graphics for the People panels, eagles and water banks; any number of Snack Bars.
The walking pro wears the body chosen in Customise.
High-resolution content packs, and tools for making your own art.
Look around while aiming on touch screens.
Points players to the CD or a CD image for the original sounds.
Reworked free graphics and sounds, and an interface overhaul.
Use the SimGolf CD itself, or a Mac .cdr image of it.
Optional extras: weather, visitors, drag to place, path styles and lamps, scorecards.
Use a CD image (.iso) of SimGolf.
Course editor, history graphs, camera controls, enhanced water, building tools and left-handed golfers.
First release.
